questions.stem: Arjun alone can finish a job in 9 days. Arjun and Lakshmi together finish it in 6 days. How many days will Lakshmi alone take?
questions.explanation: The correct option is B) 18 days. Check: 1/9 + 1/18 = 1/6 = 1/6. Work problems: add RATES (work per day), never add times.
questions.reasoning: Subtract work RATES (per day), not times. If you can eat a pizza in 3 days and your friend in 6, in ONE day you eat 1/3 and she eats 1/6; add what each does per day.

steps.text: Together per day = 1/6 = 1/6.
Arjun per day = 1/9.
Lakshmi per day = 1/6 - 1/9 = 1/18 = 1/18.
So Lakshmi alone takes 18 days.

questions.subject: LOGICAL
questions.stem: In a certain code, NETWORK is written as MDSVNQJ. How will PLANET be written in that code?
questions.explanation: The correct option is B) OKZMDS. Applying the shift to NETWORK reproduces MDSVNQJ, so the rule is consistent. Compare corresponding letters; a constant shift means every letter moves the same distance.
questions.reasoning: Compare letter positions in the alphabet to find a constant shift. Each letter jumps the same number of steps along the alphabet, like moving every pawn the same number of squares.

steps.text: N -> M: shift of 1 letters backward.
Check the other letters: all move by the same amount, so the rule is a constant shift.
Apply it to PLANET: P->O, L->K, A->Z, N->M, E->D, T->S, giving OKZMDS.

questions.subject: LOGICAL
questions.stem:
Statements:
1. Some coaches are mentors.
2. Some testers are mentors.
Conclusions:
I. No coaches are testers.
II. Some testers are coaches.
Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: The correct option is B) Neither I nor II follows. The exhaustive check of all arrangements shows I does not follow and II does not follow. 'Some' statements only guarantee existence; a conclusion must hold in every possible world, not just in one picture.
questions.reasoning: A conclusion follows only if it is true in EVERY situation that satisfies both statements. Draw circles for each group; a conclusion must be true however you could legitimately arrange the circles.

steps.text: List every possible arrangement of the three groups that keeps both statements true (160 arrangements were checked
Conclusion I (No coaches are testers.) fails in at least one of them.
Conclusion II (Some testers are coaches.) fails in at least one of them.
So the answer is: Neither I nor II follows.

questions.subject: VERBAL
questions.stem: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?

options.label: A
options.text: Mathematics does not require extra support.

options.label: B
options.text: Every employee seem confident about the result.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the managers needs more time to finish.

options.label: D
options.text: The team lead need more time to finish.

questions.answerText: Mathematics does not require extra support.
questions.explanation: The correct option is A) Mathematics does not require extra support.. 'Mathematics does not require extra support.' is the only sentence whose verb matches its subject. Find the real subject first (ignore the words in between), then match the verb.
questions.reasoning: Singular subject -> singular verb (is/has/was/needs/does); plural subject -> plural verb (are/have/were/need/do). 'Each of', 'neither of', 'every', 'everyone' and 'the number of' take singular verbs; 'a number of', 'both' and 'several' take plural verbs. A verb is a partner dancing with the subject; they must be the same size - one with one, many with many.

steps.text: Identify the subject in each sentence and decide whether it is singular or plural.
'Mathematics' is singular and takes 'does', so 'Mathematics does not require extra support.' is correct.
In the other three sentences the verb does not match the subject.

| Year | Routers | Servers | Cameras |
| 2019 | 300 | 170 | 140 |
| 2020 | 340 | 360 | 50 |

questions.explanation: The correct option is B) 7:18. 7 x 20 = 140 and 18 x 20 = 360. In DI, read the question first, pick the exact cells you need, then calculate.

Ratio = 140:360; divide both by the HCF 20.
Simplest form = 7:18.

questions.explanation: The correct option is A) 27/55. The sequential method (multiplying conditional probabilities) gives 27/55, the same value. Without replacement, the second draw depends on the first.

steps.text: Total ways to choose 2 balls = C(11,2) = 55.
Favourable ways = 27.
Probability = 27/55 = 27/55.

Conclusion I (No tailors are dancers.) fails in at least one of them.
Conclusion II (All dancers are tailors.) fails in at least one of them.
